clue.text: Like a daughter, maiden with anger

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A girl described as resembling a furious young unmarried woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as a preposition but is the definition, the verb meaning to be fond of.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them with approval, close to the verb sense of liking them.

clue.text: A sweet girl meets knight who takes flight?

parts.note: taken as written
Irma la Douce, 'Irma the sweet', is the title heroine of a French musical and film
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A lovely girl meets a knight who then runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes flight' suggests fleeing, but the answer flies aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is a pilot or crew member of an aircraft, someone who flies.

clue.text: Disclosure of fellow if leading English outpost?

parts.note: a man, a chap
taken as written
a station is a remote post or settlement, as in a colonial outpost

explanation.surface: Revealing whether a man is in charge of an English colonial outpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifestation is an outward showing or revelation of something hidden.

clue.text: Like clockwork soldier?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: steady and evenly timed
second meaning: a soldier of a standing army

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a clockwork toy soldier; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means happening at even intervals and also names a professional, full-time soldier.

clue.text: Bird at cove, flying

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is seen flying at a small bay on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: One making mark after political campaign?

definitions.meaning: on the surface someone making a name for themselves; really someone putting a cross on a paper
the campaign is the run-up to an election, after which ballots are cast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Making mark' sounds like achieving fame; here it is the cross on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A participant in an election marks a ballot paper once campaigning ends.

clue.text: Disdainful escaper from prison going down

parts.note: a con is a convict, someone who might break out of jail
descending means moving downwards

explanation.surface: A haughty jailbreaker climbs down the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Condescending means treating others with a superior, patronising air.

clue.text: Cheers affected one island

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks
to hit someone is to affect them badly, as in a region hit by floods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Applause moves one person on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is British for thank you, as is TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Grass carrying info turned and went back

indicators.note: the grass holds the other piece inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places

indicators.note: turned means the word for info is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An informer who held secret information changed sides and retreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the informer of slang, but here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or agreement.

clue.text: Take apart idlest man wandering around

indicators.note: the letters roam about and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The laziest fellow drifts about taking things to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a machine is to separate it into its component parts.

clue.text: Fish often changing in part

indicators.note: only part of these words is used, the answer sitting within them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A fish that often changes in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: It's legal, getting rid of leader — and nasty

indicators.note: getting rid of the leader means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: something that is legal is lawful

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that something is within the law yet still unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting rid of leader' drops the first letter L from LAWFUL; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad or unpleasant, a close synonym of nasty.

clue.text: Snake exhausted after cornering queen

indicators.note: the word for exhausted traps the queen within it, as if cornering her

parts.note: spent means used up or worn out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A snake, tired out after trapping a queen, perhaps on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a literary word for a snake.

clue.text: Bitter racist as horrible Conservative

indicators.note: a horrible version of the words is a mangled one, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sour, bigoted Tory is denounced as horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcastic remarks are bitter and cutting, so the adjectives overlap in tone.

clue.text: Material without embellishment — rubbish cast outside

indicators.note: the rubbish is thrown around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap, shoddy goods
bare means plain and unadorned

explanation.surface: Plain fabric is thrown out with the junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a striped upholstery fabric of silk with satin bands.

clue.text: Put an end to Highlander maybe and companion

parts.note: a Highlander is from the Scottish Highlands, one example of a Scot
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone finishes off a Highland clansman and his friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it decisively.

clue.text: Flabby guy who'd no wife unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement is a bad one, so the letters are jumbled
no means without, so the letter for wife is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fat man sadly had no wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughy describes soft, pale, flabby flesh with the texture of uncooked bread mix.

clue.text: Firm by mountain — it is in place of mineral extraction

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
an alp is a high mountain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company based beside a mountain is located at a mining site.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalpit is a mine from which coal, a mineral fuel, is dug.

clue.text: Bit from bird landing on church

indicators.note: in a down clue the bird comes to rest on top of the church, so goes first

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A fragment drops from a bird perching on a church roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or bit of something.

clue.text: Crooner joining love game

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the famous American crooner
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer of romantic ballads takes up a game of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game in which players mark off called numbers on a card.

clue.text: Rhubarb as food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nonsense, as rhubarb is used in British slang
second meaning: the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as a dish

explanation.surface: Someone serves a stalk of rhubarb as a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or empty chatter, the same as the slang sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe means both nonsensical talk and cooked cow's stomach eaten as a dish.

clue.text: Going wrong, stealing a personal decoration

indicators.note: the word for going wrong takes the letter in, as a thief takes something

parts.note: erring means making a mistake or straying
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes astray by pocketing a piece of personal jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is a piece of jewellery worn on the ear, a decoration for one's person.

clue.text: Husband with vexatious feeling finding something in wardrobe?

parts.note: anger is the feeling of being vexed

explanation.surface: A cross husband rummages and finds something in the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as one example: a wardrobe holds many things.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat hanger is a frame for hanging clothes, typically found inside a wardrobe.

clue.text: Good person, mature, with yen that's exaggerated

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword good person
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A grown-up saint with a longing behaves in an overblown way.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey describes behaviour that is theatrical and overdone, like acting on a stage.
